knowledge_point.title: Differentiating Expressions Involving the Cosecant Function

question.:question/worked-solution:
We calculate the derivative using the product rule, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{'}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x}\operatorname{csc}x) \\  & ={e}^{x}(\operatorname{csc}x)+{e}^{x}(-\operatorname{csc}x\operatorname{cot}x) \\  & ={e}^{x}\operatorname{csc}x(1-\operatorname{cot}x)\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: Real x in a connected pole-free interval (k*pi,(k+1)*pi), integer k, sin(x) != 0.

question.:question/worked-solution:
We take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\csc x-2{x}^{3}+\cos x) \\  & =(-\csc x\cot x)-2\cdot 3{x}^{2}+(-\sin x) \\  & =-\csc x\cot x-6{x}^{2}-\sin x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =-\csc \,(\frac{\pi }{4})\cot \,(\frac{\pi }{4})-6{(\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}-\sin \,(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =-\sqrt{2}\cdot 1-6\cdot \frac{{\pi }^{2}}{16}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =-\sqrt{2}-\frac{3}{8}{\pi }^{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =-\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}-\frac{3}{8}{\pi }^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: Real x in a connected pole-free interval (k*pi,(k+1)*pi), integer k, sin(x) != 0.

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\ln (x)\csc (x)) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}(\csc x)+(\ln (x))(-\csc (x)\cot (x)) \\  & =\frac{\csc (x)}{x}-\ln (x)\csc (x)\cot (x)\end{aligned}
$$
